solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: It might indicate “rat” in a French cryptic crossword, in a decorative style (3,7)

annotation.definition: It might indicate “rat” in a French cryptic crossword

blocks.clueFragment: It might indicate “rat” in a French cryptic crossword
blocks.note: in French, 'nouveau' means new, and 'new' is a standard anagram signal, so a French setter could put the word for 'art' beside it to mean rearrange ART
the ornate style of design popular around 1900

annotation.surface: A crossword setter imagines how a French colleague would clue a rodent.
annotation.walkthrough: Put 'art' with the French word for new and you have both a French-style anagram of RAT and the name of the flowing turn-of-the-century style: ART NOUVEAU.
annotation.definitionFit: The phrase names a specific movement rather than a synonym: the ornate, sinuous style of design and architecture popular around 1900.

entries.clue: Very old French impressionist briefly turned up (4)

indicatorNotes.briefly: said briefly, a word is cut short and loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.turned up: in a down entry, turning something up makes it read bottom to top

blocks.note: Edgar Degas, the French impressionist painter, without his final S

annotation.surface: An elderly French painter is carried upstairs.
annotation.walkthrough: Degas is the impressionist famous for his ballet dancers; the clue's 'Very old' also suits him, as he lived into his eighties.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone aged has lived a long time, so is very old.

entries.clue: Cunningly resist rat, one guilty of 12 Across (9)

indicatorNotes.Cunningly: done cunningly, the letters are craftily rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Someone slyly holds out against an informer.
annotation.walkthrough: 12 Across is TREASON, so the definition asks for a person who commits it; nine letters means the female form. 'Rat' in the surface is itself slang for a betrayer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by cross-reference: treason is the crime, and a woman who commits it is a traitress.

entries.clue: Fat to be set, trimming both sides (5)

indicatorNotes.trimming both sides: trimming cuts away the edges, here the first and last letters

blocks.note: TOBESET without its outer letters, the two Ts

annotation.surface: Cooking fat is left to solidify and then its edges are trimmed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fat' looks like the kitchen noun, setting in a dish; it is the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, the adjective: an obese person is very fat.

entries.clue: Meat cooked in ovens (7)

indicatorNotes.cooked: cooking turns the ingredients into something new

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: Meat is roasted in the oven.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is so plain it reads as a cookery note; 'in' belongs to the fodder, not the link.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: venison is deer meat, one kind of meat.

entries.clue: As formerly used in pesticides? (7)

blocks.note: the surface reads the ordinary word 'as'; capitalised, it is a chemical symbol
that element was a standard ingredient of insecticides and weedkillers until safer chemicals replaced it

annotation.surface: A remark about how something was once done in pest control.
annotation.walkthrough: As is the chemical symbol for ARSENIC, and the question mark flags that the little word is doing more than it seems.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by history: arsenic compounds were widely sprayed as pesticides in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

entries.clue: Shed tears when onion, say, is around (4)

indicatorNotes.is around: a word turned around runs backwards

blocks.note: an onion is an example of a bulb, hence 'say'

annotation.surface: Someone cries whenever onions are being chopped nearby.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface borrows the real reason onions make you weep.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal British: to blub is to cry, i.e. shed tears.

entries.clue: Some baffling official jargon (5)

indicatorNotes.Some: only some of the letters of the phrase are taken

blocks.note: baffLING Official

annotation.surface: Officials speak in bewildering bureaucratic language.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end, and the surface is a fair description of the answer too.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: lingo is the specialised vocabulary of a trade or group, which is what jargon is.

entries.clue: Vessel capsized by figure working around island terminus (3,7)

indicatorNotes.capsized: a capsized vessel is upside down, so in a down entry the word reads upwards
indicatorNotes.around: STAT and ON go around the I

blocks.note: SUB, a submarine, turned upside down
a stat is a statistic, a figure
I = island
on = working, as a machine is

annotation.surface: A boat overturns because someone is busy near an island's far end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Terminus' reads as the far end of the island in the surface; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a terminus is where routes end, and a bus station is where bus routes start and finish.

entries.clue: Uplift characters in chapel at evensong (5)

indicatorNotes.characters in: the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: chapEL AT Evensong

annotation.surface: Worshippers are lifted in spirit at the evening service.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like people in the congregation; it means letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: to elate someone is to lift their spirits.

entries.clue: Sling nets around chicks (9)

indicatorNotes.around: the letters are moved around into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Someone throws nets over young birds to catch them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like it describes the nets encircling the birds; it is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: nestlings are young birds not yet able to leave the nest, i.e. chicks.

entries.clue: Less weighty method of kindling fire (7)

blocks.note: the comparative of an adjective meaning not heavy
a small device that makes a flame, as for a cigarette

annotation.surface: A suggestion for starting a fire that needs less heavy gear.
annotation.walkthrough: The two halves read as one phrase; split them after 'weighty'.
annotation.definitionFit: The adjective is the comparative of light (not heavy); the noun is the pocket flame-maker, loosely a 'method' of kindling.

entries.clue: Treachery, ultimately without inducement (7)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so the last letter of the next word

blocks.note: last letter of withouT
a reason is an inducement or motive to act

annotation.surface: Someone betrays others in the end with no motive at all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like it means lacking; it only supplies its final letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: treason is betrayal of one's country, the gravest form of treachery.

entries.clue: Grand hammer and mortar (5)

blocks.note: G = grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
to hammer an opponent is to rout them

annotation.surface: A list of a builder's tools and materials.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hammer' sits beside 'mortar' as if it were a tool; it is the verb meaning to defeat heavily.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: grout is a thin mortar used to fill the gaps between tiles.

entries.clue: Omnipresent upper-class vehicle touring one South American capital (10)

indicatorNotes.touring: a bus touring a place goes all round it, so its letters surround what follows

blocks.note: U = upper-class, as in U and non-U
a bus is a vehicle; it goes around what follows
I = one, the Roman numeral
the capital of Ecuador

annotation.surface: A posh coach seems to be everywhere as it tours a South American city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One' reads as a determiner, 'one capital'; it is a letter of its own, the numeral.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something ubiquitous is found everywhere at once, which is omnipresent.

entries.clue: According to Spooner, Starmer veto for this container (4,3)

indicatorNotes.According to Spooner: Rev. Spooner was famous for swapping the starting sounds of words

blocks.note: Keir is Starmer's first name; it takes the B sound from the next word
a veto is a ban; it takes the K sound from Keir

annotation.surface: A political note about the Prime Minister blocking something.
annotation.walkthrough: Keir Starmer is the UK Labour leader and Prime Minister, so the surface's politician supplies a first name.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the answer is a metal can that holds beer, one kind of container.

entries.clue: Computer programmers drawing in primarily gifted, eccentric oldies (7)

indicatorNotes.drawing in: the outer word draws the letter inside it
indicatorNotes.primarily: primarily means first, so the first letter

blocks.note: people who write computer code
first letter of Gifted

annotation.surface: Talented software developers are recruiting quirky elderly people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gifted' looks like it describes the programmers; only its first letter is used.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal British: codgers are old men, usually thought of as odd or cantankerous, so eccentric oldies.

entries.clue: Note on puss that is to get punished (5,2)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across entry, A on B puts A after B

blocks.note: puss = cat
a chit is a short note or voucher

annotation.surface: A message pinned to the cat means it is in trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a musical letter; it is a whole short word.
annotation.definitionFit: A British idiom: you'll catch it when your mother gets home means you will be scolded or punished.

entries.clue: Icy pellet welcomes shade (9)

blocks.note: to hail someone is to greet or welcome them
a tone is a shade of colour

annotation.surface: A frozen pellet gladly receives some shelter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Welcomes' looks like a link word; it is a piece of wordplay, and a neat one beside the icy definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a hailstone is a small ball of ice falling as hail.

entries.clue: Glum is a queen over Arabic poems of mourning (7)

indicatorNotes.over: turned over, the whole string runs backwards

blocks.note: glum = sad
taken as written
Q = queen, as on playing cards

annotation.surface: A downcast queen weeps over sorrowful Arabic verse.
annotation.walkthrough: An obscure word, so trust the wordplay letter by letter; 'over' looks like 'about' in the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose definition by use: the qasida is a classical Arabic ode form, often used for elegy and lament.

entries.clue: Take in broadcast about barrier (7)

indicatorNotes.about: one word goes about, i.e. around, the other

blocks.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it
a wall is a barrier

annotation.surface: Listeners absorb a radio programme about a border wall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suggests radio; it is the old farming sense, scattering seed by hand.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to swallow food is to take it in, and to swallow a story is to believe it.

entries.clue: Donkey consuming just what is needed, a tortilla (7)

indicatorNotes.consuming: the outer word eats, i.e. contains, the inner one

blocks.note: a burro is a small donkey
'it' = just the thing, exactly what is needed

annotation.surface: A donkey eats only what it needs, which turns out to be a tortilla.
annotation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the answer is Spanish for 'little donkey'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a burrito is a flour tortilla rolled around a filling.

entries.clue: Speedy warship changes top, becoming an aggressive fighter (7)

indicatorNotes.changes top: in a down entry the top is the first letter, which is swapped for another

blocks.note: a cruiser is a fast warship; its first letter C is replaced by B

annotation.surface: A fast warship refits and becomes a battler.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter comes in; the definition and crossers show C becomes B.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a bruiser is a big, tough man who likes a fight.

entries.clue: Valuable fibre unknown in fancy tile (5)

indicatorNotes.in: X goes in the rearranged letters
indicatorNotes.fancy: fancy means elaborately worked, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: TILE rearranged
x = an unknown quantity in algebra

annotation.surface: A precious thread is found in a decorative tile.
annotation.walkthrough: An obscure word, so the wordplay must be trusted; the Toughie allows it because every letter is clued.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: ixtle is a strong fibre from Mexican agave plants, valued for cord and brushes.

entries.clue: Letter of thanks following article (5)

indicatorNotes.following: a thing following another comes after it, so the thanks goes after the article

blocks.note: the definite article
ta is British informal for thanks

annotation.surface: A thank-you note written after reading a newspaper piece.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Letter of thanks' reads as one phrase; the definition is just 'Letter', a Greek one.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

entries.clue: Hesitation admitted by a student, a group of students and an ex-student (7)

indicatorNotes.admitted by: the hesitation is let in, i.e. placed inside

blocks.note: A as written, then L = learner, as on a learner driver's plate
the sound of hesitating
the National Union of Students, the UK students' union

annotation.surface: A campus scene with a hesitant student, the students' union and a former student.
annotation.walkthrough: Three kinds of student in one clue, but only the last is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A Latin borrowing: an alumnus is a former pupil or graduate of a school or university.

entries.clue: Nick‘s drama covering end of militant Conservative (5)

indicatorNotes.covering: the drama covers, i.e. goes around, the letters
indicatorNotes.end of: the end of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: Noh is classical Japanese drama
last letter of militanT
C = Conservative

annotation.surface: A man called Nick has written a play about a hardline Tory.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nick' reads as a man's name; it is a small cut.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a nick is a small cut, and so is a notch.

entries.clue: Raised money used at first for military group (4)

indicatorNotes.Raised: in a down entry, raising a word makes it read upwards
indicatorNotes.at first: at first means the first letter

blocks.note: first letter of Used
tin is British slang for money

annotation.surface: Funds collected were spent first on an army outfit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raised money' reads as fundraising; 'Raised' is the reversal signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a unit is any organised body of troops, such as a company or battalion.

entries.clue: Exaggerates merits of measures backing series of balls (9)

indicatorNotes.backing: the measures back up, i.e. come behind, the series of balls

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a series of six balls
an ell is an old measure of cloth length

annotation.surface: Someone overstates how good certain cricket measures are.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' tempts a reversal; here it means supporting from behind, so the measures go second.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal synonym: to oversell something is to praise it beyond its real merits.

entries.clue: Point of moving north (5)

indicatorNotes.moving: the letters move into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 5 letters

annotation.surface: The purpose of heading north.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Point' reads as purpose or a compass point; it is a sharp one.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a thorn is a sharp point on a plant stem.

entries.clue: Industrial waste local lasses turned over (4)

indicatorNotes.turned over: a word turned over runs backwards

blocks.note: a dialect or informal word for girls

annotation.surface: Local girls sift through factory waste.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Local' signals a regional form of the word for girls.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: slag is the glassy waste left after smelting metal ore.

entries.clue: Most dark-hued dilapidated sweatshirt (10)

indicatorNotes.dilapidated: a dilapidated thing is falling apart, so the letters are broken up

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: A very dark, worn-out sweatshirt.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one faded garment; the first two words are the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The superlative of swarthy, which means dark-complexioned or dark in colour.
